pillar_reactions.evidence: Presented as train-as-a-unit kettlebell work, three to four sessions of 30-40 minutes, plus bespoke daily mobility protocols, with the teach-you-to-fish framing. The prospect accepted it on the education value rather than the training value: 'Well, yeah. I'm going to get an education of it. I'm going to figure it out. I'm going to learn from him' and 'six months down the road, I'm going to have an education. I may not need him any longer because I'll have the foundation to build on.' He did push back once on volume — when told three to four times a week, he corrected the record: 'I'm working out like with weights three to four times a week, and then I'm walking. I'm doing a lot of walking.'

Delivered as the standard three variables with the eating window. The prospect's response effectively neutralised the pillar: 'That's pretty much what I do now. I got the basics down, you know?' He then pre-empted the weekly indulgence himself — 'I think I have a check once a week, I'll get whatever I want once a week' — before the rep had reached it. For a prospect who already eats clean, tracks nothing, drinks black coffee and no soda, and has cut processed food, nutrition was the weakest of the three pillars and added no new value he could see.

Presented as the tailored programme, tracking app, video form feedback and Trevor's personal cell number. Prospect responded 'Yeah', 'Make sense?' 'Yes', 'I said absolutely'. This was the pillar aimed directly at his own stated gap — he had said 'I want to be accountable... I want more structure. I want results. And I want guidance' — and it drew only agreement rather than enthusiasm, because the rep presented it before making the gap hurt.

anchors.raw: I was expecting like 1,200, maybe 2,400, not 6 grand.
anchors.note: The single most actionable anchor in the batch. He arrived expecting a fifth to two-fifths of the actual price, and $1,200 is almost exactly six months of Primal University at $200 a month. Whatever brought him in set a price expectation the offer cannot meet, and the product that does meet it was never mentioned. This corroborates the sales manager's own acknowledgement on 06/22 that the price a prospect finds before the call is $200 a month or $400-$700 a month.

anchors.raw: I've taken, like I've had my personal training certifications. When I was in the department, I would get that. So I have a knowledge about how it works, you know.
anchors.note: He is himself a certified personal trainer and was his police department's wellness coordinator running bootcamp classes with kettlebells. He is not buying knowledge, he is buying structure and accountability — and the rep sold him the education value ('you're going to learn everything', 'you won't need him any longer') which is the one thing he already has.

anchors.raw: I get his feeds all the time, and, you know, recently I've been, like, walking with the kettlebell in my hand... I see his feeds come in, and I see all the kettlebell movements he's doing and stuff
anchors.note: Same pattern as the Jacob Reyf call — the prospect is already training off the coach's free content and owns the equipment. The gap between free content and $6,000 is entirely programming and accountability, and nobody named that gap out loud.

anchors.raw: I have a home gym here where I got my kettlebells, I got my bands and my pull-up tower, whatever.
anchors.note: Fifteen years of kettlebell familiarity plus a fully equipped home gym. Removes any equipment cost from the value stack and narrows what he is actually paying for.

anchors.raw: I got other things I'm paying on right now, which I have to complete before I get myself further in debt, especially where I'm on a fixed income
anchors.note: Not a negotiating position — a stated constraint with a named horizon. He said twice that the debts clear 'in a matter of months' and that he 'would be able to' then. That is a follow-up date the rep did not take.

anchors.raw: I do have supplements I take, you know, some, but even that I want to cut, I think I want to cut that back because I'm starting to think like a lot of them are just just a waste of time, you know, it's just marketing and it's a gimmick
anchors.note: A general and freshly stated distrust of fitness-industry marketing claims, volunteered twenty minutes before he was asked for $6,000. Nothing in the presentation was adjusted for it.

anchors.raw: I can't justify spending that much money on myself, you know? Especially when I already know what I'm doing.
anchors.note: Two separate objections compressed into one sentence — a self-worth barrier to spending on himself, and the competence anchor of already knowing what he is doing. Neither was addressed.

unmet_demand.want: An entry point at the $1,200-$2,400 he expected to pay
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Primal University exists at $200 a month, which is within a few hundred dollars of the bottom of his expected range across six months. It was never mentioned on this call, even after four declines. The rep instead spent the last eight minutes trying to reach $6,000 from a prospect who had told him he was on a fixed income.

unmet_demand.want: A start date timed to when his current debts clear
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He offered it twice — 'a couple of things I'm paying on now that will be paid up in a matter of months, and then I would be able to.' The rep did not acknowledge it, did not ask how many months, and did not book anything.

unmet_demand.want: To know what the payment options actually are before disclosing his personal finances
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He asked plainly — 'What's the options?' — and was told 'We don't have anything set in stone. It always differs from the particular person', with disclosure made conditional on him going first. There is a real answer available; the same rep laid out four concrete structures for another prospect the previous day.

unmet_demand.want: Assurance that a programme built on ballistic kettlebell work is appropriate for an L3-L4-L5 fusion and an unrecovered triceps tear still under investigation
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Never raised by either party after the initial injury question. The prospect volunteered that a clinician had previously told him his lifting days were over, and has a specialist appointment the next day, and neither fact was connected to the purchase.

unmet_demand.want: Instruction on specific technical movements he has watched but cannot perform, such as the windmill
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Genuinely served by the programme and the closest thing to a clean product-fit on this call. Recorded because it is his most concrete want and the presentation spent more time on nutrition, which he already does well, than on the movement library he actually came for.
